mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in RETAIL_REC mobility observed at t-0w indicates a strong negative momentum driven by reduced non-essential outings, which will persist and further depress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, or shows a sustained recovery within the period.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding 10 percentage points, signals a widespread shift to remote work, directly reducing foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 10 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not fall further, despite WORKPLACES mobility dropping by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility and decrease in TRANSIT usage indicates a strong and reinforcing stay-at-home behavior, which will severely depress RETAIL_REC as people avoid public spaces and non-essential travel over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT falls at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite concurrent increases in RESIDENTIAL and decreases in TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp, widespread declines across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES at t-0w are direct consequences of impending or recently enacted government stay-at-home orders, which will enforce a sustained reduction in non-essential retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant recovery, indicating that policy measures did not effectively suppress non-essential activity.

mechanism_narrative: While GROCERY_PHARM mobility is rising due to essential needs and potential panic buying, this activity is distinct from leisure, causing RETAIL_REC to continue its decline as non-essential outings are curtailed over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC falls at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases, despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing to rise and RETAIL_REC having fallen sharply at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: As indoor retail and recreation options become restricted, people will increasingly seek outdoor alternatives like parks. A rebound in PARKS mobility after a dip will indicate this shift, further depressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as leisure time is reallocated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases week-on-week at t+1w, following the decline observed at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, despite PARKS mobility showing a rebound, suggesting no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and substantial week-on-week decline in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility signifies a collapse in daily commuting patterns, which will directly and severely reduce foot traffic to retail and recreation businesses over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by more than 10 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows an increase, despite significant concurrent drops in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating people are spending significantly more time at home, directly correlates with reduced engagement in external retail and recreation activities, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility is above 5% change from baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining significantly elevated.
